<!-- pr-reviewer: d8f4c65dbd83609da5f74aeb8073421202075969 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- `then` (carry.rs, new fn): m' = b*a, xy shift = b*t_self + t_next, z = s_next*t_self.z + t_next.z, s' = s*s'. I checked each against `apply` by hand; it equals `next.apply(self.apply(p))`. Associativity follows from it being a composition of affine maps. Entries are in {-1,0,1}, so the i8 products cannot overflow.
- `unapply` reuses `back_xy` (transpose of an orthogonal m) and `s*(z - t.z)`; `s` is its own inverse. It is correct for all 8 turns.
- Handedness: `LatticeTurn` can only be built by `from_matrix`, which demands det(m)*s == 1, so no mirror can enter. Composition keeps det = 1 and so cannot produce one either.
- The carried view is the pure `field.distance(unapply(p))`, so sign and magnitude are preserved (rigid invariance). `mesh_distance` and `inside` do the same. No cells, bricks or origin offsets are touched; the field's own lookups run in its own frame, so there is no off-by-one or odd/even-extent exposure in this step. (The lattice-origin question belongs to step B when `carry::Body` is wired.)
- No unwrap/expect/panic in src; test-only `expect`/`panic!` are allowed. Provenance lines present. Behaviour-neutral, no golden change.

**Local results (trial-merged with upstream/main; only AGENTS.md differs from the PR base)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (full) | 45 suites, 349 passed, 0 failed (lib 65, field_carry 3, stock_carry 7, stock_backend_parity 13, stock_columns 3) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The `unapply` doc says "`unapply(apply(p)) == p` bit for bit". That holds for the integer-valued shifts the tests use, but with a fractional `t` the `+t`/`-t` round trip can differ by 1 ulp. Likewise `then` vs sequential application can differ by an ulp for fractional shifts. Consider softening the wording to "exact up to rounding of the shift".
2. `mod field_carry;` sits before `field_blade`/`field_bull` in `stock_sim/mod.rs`; `cargo fmt` would reorder it (same for the `pub use`).
3. The PR has no `Fixes`, which is right for `Refs`. The body has the `Changelog:` line.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Delta review** of the merge(s) since the last reviewed head d8f4c65 (head now 581cbc5). The author added only merge-of-main / stack-merge commits, no new own code.

Checked:
- Resolution: merge of main (581cbc53, 4827fde6 into the branch): the only conflict was the module list in crates/sim/src/stock_sim/mod.rs; both sides kept (main's mod field_box and this PR's mod field_carry). Nothing from main dropped; the head already contains current main (4827fde6).
- Diff vs main lists only this PR's own files (crates/sim and, for the last of the stack, its docs/decisions file); no snapshot PNG, CHANGELOG.md or RECOMMENDED.md edits; nothing outside crates/sim differs from main.
- Gate (merged with main, own worktree and target): camcraft-sim lib 65 passed; field_carry, stock_carry and the stack's own test binaries all passed (counts: lib 65, field_carry 3, stock_carry 7); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Result: the earlier clean review still holds. This PR is stacked, so it merges parent first.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
